learn.title: Solar PV Panel Electricity Generation
learn.intro: Solar panels convert sunlight into electricity using the photoelectric effect, a key technology for decarbonizing power generation. Understanding this process helps explain how clean energy scales globally. With over 90 GW of solar installed in India alone, mastering this concept is vital for energy literacy.
learn.c1_text: When photons strike a PV cell, they knock electrons loose from semiconductor material like silicon. This creates a flow of electricity, similar to how wind turns a turbine blade. Each photon transfers energy to an electron, initiating current flow in the cell.
learn.c2_text: Silicon cells have a positive and negative layer (p-n junction) creating an electric field. When photons hit the junction, electrons move toward the positive side, generating DC current. Inverters then convert DC to AC for grid use, enabling homes and businesses to harness sunlight.
learn.c3_text: India's Bhadla Solar Park in Rajasthan spans 14,000 acres with 2.25 GW capacity, showcasing large-scale PV deployment. Government policies like accelerated depreciation and solar tenders have driven rapid growth, making solar the fastest-growing energy sector in the nation.

learn.title: Building Integrated Photovoltaics (BIPV)
learn.intro: BIPV integrates solar panels into building materials, merging energy generation with architecture. This approach reduces costs and enhances aesthetics, crucial for urban solar adoption. With India's 200 GW renewable target by 2030, BIPV offers scalable rooftop and façade solutions for dense cities.
learn.c1_text: BIPV uses solar tiles, windows, or roofing shingles instead of traditional panels. These materials generate power while serving as building components. For example, solar glass can power offices, while PV roofs replace conventional tiles, saving installation costs by up to 30% compared to add-on systems.
learn.c2_text: BIPV reduces building energy use by generating power on-site, cutting transmission losses. Combined with insulation and smart glass, it optimizes thermal regulation. Studies show BIPV can reduce net energy consumption by 25-40% in commercial buildings, enhancing sustainability certifications like LEED.
learn.c3_text: Infosys Campus in Bangalore uses BIPV façades generating 2.5 MW, powering 10,000 employees. The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy's 'Solar Parks Scheme' supports BIPV integration. By 2030, India aims for 20% rooftop solar, with BIPV key to achieving urban energy goals.
learn.stat4: BIPV cost reduction: 30% vs add-on panels

learn.title: Sodium-Ion Batteries: Lithium Alternative
learn.intro: Sodium-ion batteries offer a cost-effective, abundant alternative to lithium-ion for grid storage. Their raw material abundance and lower production costs make them critical for expanding renewable energy systems. With India's battery demand expected to reach 500 GWh by 2030, sodium-ion presents a strategic opportunity for local manufacturing.
learn.c1_text: Sodium is 10,000 times more abundant than lithium in Earth's crust. Sodium-ion batteries use similar tech to lithium but with cheaper materials like sodium titanate. While energy density is 15-20% lower, their lifespan exceeds 5,000 cycles, ideal for daily grid cycling applications.
learn.c2_text: Sodium-ion costs are projected at $80/kWh vs lithium's $150/kWh by 2030. They perform well in extreme temperatures (-40°C to 80°C), reducing cooling needs. Their simpler manufacturing process enables rapid scaling, with China leading production. India's 'Make in India' initiative aims to localize battery supply chains.
learn.c3_text: Indian startups like Surya Roshan and Tata Chemicals are piloting sodium-ion projects. The National Mission on Strategic Technologies funds R&D for indigenous battery tech. With 70% of lithium imports coming from politically sensitive regions, sodium-ion reduces import dependence for India's 500 GW renewable target.

learn.title: Wind Resource Assessment Methods
learn.intro: Wind resource assessment identifies optimal sites for turbines using meteorological data and modeling. Accurate assessments maximize energy yield and reduce project risks. With India's 60 GW wind target by 2030, precise site evaluation is crucial for unlocking India's 180 GW technical wind potential.
learn.c1_text: Assessment uses anemometers, lidar, and satellite data to measure wind speed/direction at 100m height. Software models predict energy yield using Weibull distributions. For example, a site with 8 m/s average wind speed generates 2,500 kWh/MW/year, while 6 m/s yields 1,200 kWh/MW/year, guiding turbine placement decisions.
learn.c2_text: Advanced tools like WAsP and OpenWind analyze turbulence, air density, and terrain effects. Turbine hub height and rotor size are optimized for local conditions. Offshore sites require additional wave/current data. Studies show proper assessment improves energy output by 10-15%, directly impacting project ROI.
learn.c3_text: India's top wind corridors include Gujarat's Kutch region (9 m/s average), Tamil Nadu Coonamore, and Rajasthan's Jaisalmer. The Ministry's 'National Wind Resource Function' maps 216 km² of potential sites. Recent auctions like the 440 MW Gopalganj project in Bihar highlight growing assessment rigor for utility-scale development.

learn.title: Iron-Air Batteries for Long-Duration Storage
learn.intro: Iron-air batteries store energy for 100+ hours using abundant iron and air, addressing grid-scale storage needs. Their low cost and longevity make them ideal for balancing renewables. With global long-duration storage demand at 30,000 GWh by 2050, India's 500 GWh storage target necessitates technologies like iron-air.
learn.c1_text: During discharge, iron oxidizes to iron oxide while oxygen from air reduces at the cathode. Charging reverses the process using renewable energy. These batteries achieve 90% round-trip efficiency and operate for decades without degradation. Energy density reaches 1,000 Wh/kg, enabling cost-effective multi-day storage.
learn.c2_text: Iron-air systems provide frequency regulation, peak shaving, and renewable firming. A 100 MWh iron-air plant can replace 20 MW gas peakers, saving $15M annually in fuel costs. Their 100+ hour duration supports seasonal storage, complementing solar/wind by storing excess summer generation for winter use.
learn.c3_text: India's Green Energy Corridors prioritize long-duration storage. The 10 GW/120 GWh BESS target includes iron-air research under the Department of Science. Projects like the 10 MWh iron-air pilot in Gujarat's Dholera demonstrate potential for agricultural and industrial microgrids, aligning with India's 2030 renewable export goals.

learn.title: Solid-State Battery Technology
learn.intro: Solid-state batteries replace liquid electrolytes with ceramics or polymers, enhancing safety and energy density. This innovation is critical for EVs and grid storage. With India's EV target of 30% sales by 2030, solid-state batteries could double driving range while eliminating fire risks, accelerating adoption.
learn.c1_text: Solid electrolytes prevent dendrite formation and thermal runaway, common in lithium-ion. They enable higher voltage (4.5V vs 3.7V) and energy density (500 Wh/kg vs 250 Wh/kg). For example, Toyota's prototype achieves 1,000 Wh/kg, allowing 1,000 km range in 15 minutes charging, transforming EV usability.
learn.c2_text: Producing uniform solid electrolytes at scale requires precision. Techniques like thin-film deposition and cold sintering are being optimized. Companies like QuantumScape report 800 cycles before degradation. Cost projections show $100/kWh by 2030, making them competitive with conventional batteries for grid applications.
learn.c3_text: IISc Bangalore and Tata Chemicals collaborate on ceramic electrolytes using local materials. The $2.5B National Mission on Interdisciplinary Cyber-Physical Systems funds 50+ startups. India's EV policy incentivizes R&D, with plans for 10 GWh solid-state production capacity by 2030 to support automotive exports.
